- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early/medium horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates or lags behind true price movements; increase forecast slightly, especially in late horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% for 3–7 day horizon.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in 10–30 day horizon — if forecast is significantly above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% for next 10 days.
- Sentiment spikes (e.g., 1.0) followed by low sentiment (0.0–0.2) often trigger model to overcorrect; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for 3–5 days after sentiment drop.
- In 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true price by 1–4% when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment is ≤0.4.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.0–0.2 values, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–2% for 5–10 day horizon to catch momentum.
